task.title: balanced-brackets
task.statement: The brackets package exposes is_bracket (already implemented) and a stub is_balanced(s). Implement is_balanced(s) so that it returns True when the three kinds of brackets (), [] and {} in the string s are correctly matched and nested, and False otherwise. Characters that are not brackets are ignored. The empty string is balanced. is_balanced must return a bool. Raise TypeError when s is not a string. Do not change is_bracket or the tests.
acceptance_criteria: nested mixed brackets with other characters are balanced: '(a[b]{c})', 'f(x[0], y[1])'
non-bracket characters are ignored
is_balanced returns a bool

spec.restated_task: Implement is_balanced(s) in brackets/core.py, available through from brackets import is_balanced, to determine whether the ASCII brackets (), [] and {} in a string are correctly matched and nested. Ignore every other character, treat empty strings and strings without brackets as balanced, always return a bool for string inputs, and raise TypeError for non-string inputs. Preserve is_bracket and the existing tests.

interface_contract.name: brackets.is_balanced
interface_contract.behavior: Accept str instances, including subclasses. Process the six ASCII bracket characters in their original order, ignoring all other characters. Return True exactly when every closing bracket matches the most recent unmatched opening bracket and no opening brackets remain unmatched at the end. Otherwise return False. Return values must be actual bool instances. Empty strings and strings containing no brackets return True. Quotes, escapes, and other text do not suppress bracket processing.
error_cases: TypeError: s is not an instance of str; do not coerce or iterate non-string inputs. No particular exception message is required.

interface_contract.name: brackets.is_bracket
interface_contract.behavior: Preserve the existing implementation: return True exactly when c is a str instance of length one containing one of (, ), [, ], {, or }; return False otherwise.

acceptance_criteria: 1. from brackets import is_balanced and from brackets import is_bracket both succeed.
2. is_balanced returns True for each of '', '()', '[]', '{}', '()[]{}', and '([{}])'.
3. is_balanced returns True for '(a[b]{c})' and 'f(x[0], y[1])'.
4. is_balanced returns False for each of '(', ')', '([)]', '(]', '{[}', and '())'.
5. Closing brackets without preceding unmatched opening brackets are rejected: ')(', '][', and '}{' each return False.
6. Unmatched opening brackets remaining after otherwise valid pairs are rejected: '(()', '[[]', and '{{}' each return False.

7. All non-bracket characters, including whitespace, newlines, Unicode characters, quotes, and backslashes, are ignored. For every string s, its result equals the result for s with all characters outside '()[]{}' removed.
8. Strings containing no ASCII brackets, including 'abc', whitespace-only strings, and '你好（）', return True.
9. For every string input, the result has type bool, rather than an integer or another truthy or falsy object.
10. str subclass instances are accepted and evaluated by the same bracket-matching rules.
11. Non-string inputs, including None, True, 0, 1.5, b'()', ['(', ')'], ('(', ')'), {}, and set(), raise TypeError.
12. Repeated calls are independent: a call returning False or raising TypeError does not affect later calls with balanced strings.
13. is_bracket retains its existing behavior: each character in '()[]{}' returns True; 'a', '', '((', and 1 return False. Its implementation remains unchanged.
14. Existing test files remain unchanged and their tests continue to pass.
out_of_scope: Changing is_bracket, PAIRS, OPEN, CLOSE, or package exports.
Adding bracket types beyond the six ASCII bracket characters.
Parsing programming-language syntax or treating quoted or escaped brackets specially.
Adding dependencies, new public APIs, or input coercion.

sealed_tests.notes: Covers matching order, ignored characters, exact bool results, string subclasses, TypeError cases, call independence, and existing is_bracket behavior.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code and is the first step of its branch; two verifier canaries detect blanket result forgery. A candidate can still forge its own result from inside a child after the nonce was read if it spares the canaries (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

The repository's own suite and the held-out suite run after the sealed verification in their own branches. They are bound through the same supervisor only for unittest repositories whose tests are statically discoverable; otherwise they are parsed from console output and the gate is labelled evidence_class 'stdout'.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter then classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, corrects and re-verifies them (must pass on the candidate and still fail on the base). Arbitration is advisory by default and never clears an implementation bug or a contract dispute; it changes the verdict only in explicit apply mode.
Grounding runs only when the specification names external references; sources are cited, not verified for correctness.
Sandbox CPU/RAM quota controls were not found in the current public REST API; per operation only max_layer_bytes, a timeout and the networking flag are set.
Sandbox raw 'cost' diagnostics are not USD; Codex gateway usage is ChatGPT allowance, not a Nebius charge; Nebius USD is computed from the public price table, not an invoice.
